subject: business-studies
title: Portfolio Balance
welcome_lead: Why a balanced portfolio of products beats one big bet.
meta_desc: A-Level Portfolio: balance across the BCG quadrants.
final_note: Healthy firms keep cash cows feeding stars and pruning dogs.

concepts.def: Today's question marks become tomorrow's stars then cows.
Selling or closing a business unit.
Removing weak products to focus resources.
Value created when products share resources.
New products eating sales of existing ones.

walkthroughs.body_html: Successful products march from question mark through star to cash cow, sometimes ending as a dog. A firm with no question marks today has no stars tomorrow.
Dogs absorb management attention out of proportion to revenue. Divestment frees capital and focus. Some dogs deserve protection - loss leaders that draw traffic to better products.
Shared brands, channels and R&D create synergy. A portfolio of unrelated products often disappoints - conglomerate discounts on stock markets reflect this.

mcqs.q: Why does a company's share price change?
options: Share prices go up when a company makes more money this year.
Share prices are set by the government each morning.
Share prices reflect investors' expectations about future profits — driven by company performance, sector trends, economic conditions, and market sentiment.

mcqs.q: What is corporate governance, and how does it differ from CSR?
options: Corporate governance is the same as corporate social responsibility.

Corporate governance is the system of rules, practices and processes by which a company is directed and controlled — focusing on accountability, board structure and shareholder rights. CSR is about wider social/environmental responsibility.

mcqs.q: What is Herzberg's distinction between hygiene factors and motivators?
options: Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness.
Corporate governance is the legal requirement to have a CEO.
Higher pay always motivates employees.
Hygiene factors (pay, conditions, policies) prevent dissatisfaction when present but don't motivate; motivators (recognition, achievement, responsibility) create positive satisfaction.
